key_insight: AVS-HOBO reuses previously invalid states in a cyclic mapping, removing one penalty term and making VQE more reliable for constrained optimization on NISQ hardware.
engineering_relevance: The encoding offers a more practical quantum formulation for TSP-style problems, improving feasibility and scalability for near-term quantum optimization workflows.
method: Construct a higher-order binary optimization Hamiltonian for TSP with an efficient binary representation.
Introduce an all-valid-state HOBO (AVS-HOBO) scheme that eliminates one penalty term via cyclic mapping.
Test VQE on noiseless simulations and real quantum hardware, including error-mitigation comparisons.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate TSP instances up to 20 cities and compare original HOBO vs. AVS-HOBO using energy convergence, approximation, tour-length, and feasibility ratios on simulators and multiple real devices.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on hardware architecture and error-mitigation choice, so results may not transfer uniformly across all NISQ platforms.
paper_title: All-valid-state HOBO encoding for constrained combinatorial optimization on NISQ devices
